newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European stocks move higher, dollar soft.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European stocks move higher, dollar soft.

text.p: European bourses turned higher on Friday morning, led by London's FTSE-100 index, which reversed opening losses to reach a record high.
The dollar remained soft after prospects faded on Thursday for any imminent U.S. rate increase. But activity is expected to remain subdued with U.S. markets closed for the Independence Day holiday.

Gold markets worldwide were braced for possible further falls, after news that the Australian central bank had sold a large chunk of its reserves knocked prices to 12-year lows of around $323 an ounce.
The FTSE-100 index opened slightly lower but climbed to a record high of 4,879 early, led by the derivatives market.

Investors who had sold short the index futures were being forced to buy them back in what is known as a "short-squeeze" situation. As that buying pushes futures prices up, arbitrageurs surface to close the gap that emerges between prices on the futures index and the underlying market, resulting in a rise in both markets.
But gains could be limited if the early buying remains a technical move and dries up.
As the FTSE-100 rose, other European bourses followed. Paris' CAC-40 index briefly turned up but struggled to hold gains, with brokers saying the market needed to consolidate recent gains.

The blue-chip French index was also buoyed by a surge in Canal Plus after the pay-TV group said on Friday it expected to generate a 1997 profit of three billion francs ($508.5 million), instead of breaking even, after two transactions with the Kirch Group.
The two deals include selling its 37.5-percent stake in Germany's Premiere to Kirch and buying Kirch's 45-percent stake in Italy's Telepiu.
At 0850 GMT, Canal shares were up more than two percent at 1,245 French francs.
Valeo also rose after a 14.6 percent rise in first-half sales and forecasts for higher results when it reports on July 16.
Just before 0900 GMT, Valeo was up nearly three percent at 399.30 francs, just off its new high of 402.00.
Before bourse trading opened, Germany's IBIS DAX index started to pare losses in electronic trading in line with the overnight surge on Wall Street and the FTSE-100's early jump to an all-time high.
That slow rise, begun in electronic trading, continued into bourse trading so when exchange trading started, the DAX was well on its way to its own record high at 3,944.51.
The Dow soared 100.43 points on Thursday to close at a record high 7,895.81 after a smaller rise than expected in U.S. payrolls in June confirmed moderating growth amid low inflation.

But the bullish report for U.S. stocks dampened the dollar. The dollar slipped on perceptions the Federal Reserve (Fed) would not have to raise U.S. rates at its next policy-making meeting in August to rein in growth and inflation.
The dollar's softness lingered into early European trading on Friday, hitting a one-week low against the yen.

"The upside risk for growth is in Japan, not the U.S., and given that the Fed may not have to raise rates in the second half of this year, it looks like dollar/yen will be in a bit of trouble," said Ian Morris, international economist at HSBC Markets.
Against the mark, the dollar fared better, partly due to the German currency's fall to nearly the lowest level this year against the yen.

"The only thing that will help the mark right now is the complete collapse of EMU (economic and monetary union)," said Gerard Lyons, DKB chief economist. "Given that looks very unlikely, mark/yen is a one-way bet."
EMU is seen hurting the mark because the planned single currency expected to replace participants' national currencies is expected to be softer than Germany's currency now.
CURRENCIES AT 0920 GMT
The dollar was at 113.28 yen and 1.7502 marks comapred with 113.45 and 1.7495 in late Europe on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0920 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 6.3 points at 4,838.00.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 4.75 at 2,932.23.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 52.27 at 3939.66.
PRECIOUS METALS
London gold opened at 324.25, sharply lower than $331.50 an ounce at Thursday's close. Silver opened lower at $4.57, down from $4.65 at Thursday's close.
($ = 5.9 French Francs)
